To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Diminished levels of sRAGE are associated with poor survival in melanoma, which is in line with a recent report by our group.”
diminished serum levels of the soluble forms of the RAGE receptor are prognostic for poor outcome in melanoma patients.
the soluble forms of the RAGE receptor (sRAGE, esRAGE) and variants in its promoter are associated with poor survival in melanoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prognostic role of sRAGE, esRAGE and SNPs in the genetic locus of RAGE in malignant melanoma patients.
the identification of prognostic markers and their underlying mechanisms for melanoma patients with poor prognosis.
a novel biomarker for melanoma prognosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RAGE is a prognostic marker in melanoma and is a potential target for therapeutic intervention in this disease.
RAGE and its soluble forms are promising prognostic markers in melanoma patients.
the soluble forms of the RAGE receptor are prognostic biomarkers for the survival of melanoma patients with a high risk for progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sRAGE and the RAGE SNPs are prognostic for OS and PFS.
RAGE is a prognostic marker for melanoma patients with poor prognosis.

RAGE is upregulated in melanomas and the soluble forms of the receptor, which are produced by the receptor itself and/or by other cells in the tumor microenvironment, can be measured in the blood and are prognostic for survival in melanomas with high risk for metastasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sRAGE and its genetic polymorphisms are associated with survival in high risk melanoma patients.
the soluble forms of the receptor for advanced glycation end products are prognostic biomarkers for survival in melanom patients with high risk of disease progression.
